note: The attacker-controlled \u0000 escape inside a quoted JSON key is decoded by ucl_unescape_json_string into a raw NUL byte written into the key buffer (uval==0). The function still returns the full unescaped length (t - str) that includes this NUL byte, so the logical key contains an embedded NUL and is longer than its NUL-terminated prefix.

The parser stores the full unescaped key length (including the embedded NUL) on the object and points nobj->key at the unescaped buffer held in nobj->trash_stack[UCL_TRASH_KEY]. The key is only NUL-terminated at its logical end, not before it.

The `.inherit "defaults"` macro iterates the children of the top-level 'defaults' object. The child whose key contains the embedded NUL is passed to ucl_object_copy, which deep-copies it through ucl_object_copy_internal.

Root cause: the key copy uses strdup, treating the key as a NUL-terminated C string instead of copying other->keylen bytes. Because the key contains an embedded NUL, strdup stops there, so the freshly allocated key buffer is shorter than the key length that was memcpy'd into new at line 3585.

new->key is pointed at the truncated strdup'd buffer while new->keylen still holds the full original length (including the embedded NUL), creating a key pointer / keylen mismatch on the copied object.

When the copied element is itself an object, each of its children (copied recursively, so their keys are likewise truncated by strdup) is inserted into the copy with the truncated key pointer together with the full keylen. The reported out-of-bounds read inside ucl_object_copy_internal occurs in the key processing of this insert call.

Sink: the loop `for (p = key; p < key + keylen; p ++)` dereferences keylen bytes of the truncated strdup'd key buffer; reading past the short allocation is a heap out-of-bounds read of size 1. Reached from ucl_object_copy_internal line 3622 (nested object keys) or from ucl_inherit_handler line 1951 (scalar keys).
